deep.reconstruction:
This folio contains no mathematics. It is a page of lecture or study notes on ancient (biblical) Jewish history, written in German Kurrent. It continues directly from the previous page, which treats the period of the Judges and ends with Samuel and the demand for a king. The hand and content suggest student notes from a history course; there is no evidence on this page that it was written by Gauss.

Content, step by step:

(1) Heading 'Dritte Periode' (Third Period): from Saul to the fall of the Jewish state and the deportation into the Babylonian captivity. Marginal heading: 'Periode der Monarchie' (period of the monarchy), dated 1100–600 BC.

(2) The period divides into two parts:
- I. 1095–975, when Israel remained undivided.
- II. 975–590, when the kingdom split into Juda and Israel.

(3) Subsection a: 'Der jüdische Staat als ein Reich' (the Jewish state as a single kingdom), 1100–975.

(4) In this period three kings reigned, each for 40 years: Saul, David and Solomon.

(5) Saul's reign:
- Saul was made king with great solemnity.
- From the start he faced a large party against him.
- He won a great victory over the Ammonites and so gained respect.
- Samuel then laid down his judicial office. The next words are hard to read.
- Samuel's influence nevertheless continued: he remained intermediary ('Mittelsperson') between the king and Jehovah. This sentence continues on the next page.

The only quantitative content is chronology. Three reigns of 40 years give 120 years, which matches 1095 − 975 = 120. The next page gives Saul's death as c. 1055, and 1095 − 1055 = 40, consistent with his 40-year reign. Part II spans 975 − 590 = 385 years.
errors: The heading gives the monarchy's start as 1100 (and subsection a as 1100–975), but part I starts at 1095. This is a minor internal inconsistency of 5 years.
The end date of the period is given as 600 in the heading but 590 in part II. Both are rounded; modern chronology puts the fall of Jerusalem in 587/586 BC.

Forty-year reigns for each of the three kings follow the traditional biblical numbers (Saul's 40 years comes from Acts 13:21). This is not historically secure, but it was standard in textbooks of the period.

results.what: Periodization of Israelite history: united monarchy 1095–975 under three kings of 40 years each, then the divided kingdom 975–590
results.modern_name: Traditional biblical chronology of the United and Divided Monarchy
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th/early-19th-century universal-history textbooks (e.g. Göttingen school historians), following biblical chronology

deep.surprise_reason: The page is non-mathematical history lecture notes repeating standard biblical chronology. Nothing here bears on Gauss's mathematics, and it may not even be in his hand.

checkable.asserts: The undivided kingdom (1095–975) equals three reigns of 40 years each.
Length of the divided-kingdom period as stated.
Saul's death c. 1055 (next page) is consistent with a 40-year reign starting 1095.

transcription_corrections: 'Jüdische{+r+}[?] Periode haben 3 Könige regiert' should read 'In dieser Periode haben 3 Könige regiert, jeder 40 Jahr'.
'zum König gewählt[?]' could equally be 'zum König ernannt'; the ending is unclear.
'[-Ammoniter-][?]' is a marginal insertion in red ink, and 'Ammoniter' is the correct reading.
'Er hielt[?] Mittel gegen[?] zwischen dem' should read 'Er blieb Mittelsperson zwischen dem', which continues onto the next page with 'König und dem Jehovah.'
'Nun erlegte Samuel' is 'Nun er-|legte' split across a line break, i.e. 'Nun legte Samuel sein richterliches Amt nieder'. The following words ('und selbst zu gewinnen machte') remain uncertain.
'Periode der Monarchie' is written above the line as an insertion into the heading.
